extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, small business inventors, USPTO policymakers, and legislators
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts statutory provisions and procedural standards in the America Invents Act (as amended in the managers' amendment) governing examination, fees, post-grant review, small-entity treatment, USPTO funding, and related patent-administration rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Ombudsman Program for Small Business Concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to available resources, the Director may establish in the United States Patent and Trademark Office a Patent Ombudsman Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duties of the Program’s staff shall include providing support and services relating to patent filings to small business concerns. (Purpose: provide a fast lane within USPTO to receive information and assistance regarding patent applications.)

rubrics_metrics.name: First-inventor-to-file system and 1-year grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition the patent system from a first-to-invent system to a first-inventor-to-file system; use the filing date of an application to determine the true inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The change is intended to increase predictability and speed. The bill still provides a safe harbor of a year for inventors to go out and market their inventions before having to file for their patents (the 'grace period'), protecting disclosures by professors and others who discuss or publish before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions and post-grant challenges to improve examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow third parties to provide information to the patent examiner and provide a modernized, streamlined mechanism for third parties to challenge recently issued, low-quality patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: bridge the information gap between the patent application and existing knowledge and eliminate low-quality patents that should not have been issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO fee-setting authority and cost-recovery requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall have authority to set or adjust by rule any fee established, authorized, or charged under title 35 and the Trademark Act of 1946 for all services performed by or materials furnished by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided that patent and trademark fee amounts are in the aggregate set to recover the estimated cost to the Office for processing, activities, services, and materials relating to patents and trademarks, respectively, including proportionate shares of the administrative costs of the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority examination fee reduction for small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall reduce fees for providing prioritized examination of utility and plant patent applications by 50 percent for small entities that qualify for reduced fees under section 41(h)(1) of title 35, United States Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition: so long as the fees of the prioritized examination program are set to recover the estimated cost of the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary injunction timing limitation where petition for post-grant review filed
rubrics_metrics.description: If a civil action alleging infringement of a patent is filed within 3 months of the grant of the patent, the court may not stay its consideration of the patent owner’s motion for a preliminary injunction on the basis that a petition for post-grant review has been filed or that such a proceeding has been instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits using post-grant review petitions as a procedural basis to delay preliminary relief shortly after grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of transitional post-grant review for covered business-method patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall issue regulations establishing and implementing a transitional post-grant review proceeding for review of the validity of covered business-method patents, to be issued not later than 1 year after enactment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transitional proceeding shall be regarded as and employ the standards and procedures of a post-grant review under chapter 32, subject to specified exceptions and qualifications (see related subcriteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on petitions for transitional CBM proceedings (standing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may not file a petition for a transitional proceeding with respect to a covered business-method patent unless the person or his real party in interest has been sued for infringement of the patent or has been charged with infringement under that patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standing is limited to parties who have been sued or charged with infringement (i.e., litigants/defendants), not general third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted prior-art bases in transitional CBM proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner who challenges claims in a covered business-method patent on a ground raised under section 102 or 103 (as in effect on the day prior to enactment) may support such ground only on the basis of prior art described by section 102(a) (as in effect before enactment) or prior art that (I) discloses the invention more than 1 year prior to the U.S. application and (II) would be described by section 102(a) (pre-enactment) if disclosed by another before the applicant's invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits the types of prior art that can be invoked in transitional CBM proceedings to older statutory categories or year-old disclosures satisfying certain conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel from re-asserting grounds raised in transitional proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner (or his real party in interest) may not assert in a civil action under section 1338 or in an ITC proceeding that a claim in a patent is invalid on any ground that the petitioner raised during a transitional proceeding that resulted in a final written decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a preclusion/estoppel rule preventing relitigation of grounds adjudicated in the transitional proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and definition of 'covered business method patent' (CBM)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the transitional program, 'covered business method patent' means a patent that claims a method or corresponding apparatus for performing data processing operations utilized in the practice, administration, or management of a financial product or service, except that the term shall not include patents for technological inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solely for implementing the transitional proceeding, the Director shall prescribe regulations for determining whether a patent is for a technological invention (i.e., exclusions for technological inventions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional CBM effective date and sunset
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations implementing the transitional proceeding shall take effect 1 year after enactment and apply to all covered business-method patents issued before, on, or after such date of enactment, with specified exceptions; the transitional program (and its regulations) shall be repealed 4 years after the regulations take effect, but shall continue to apply to any petition filed prior to repeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the timeline and limited duration (sunset) for transitional CBM proceedings and preserves applicability to petitions filed before repeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court stay request factors for transitional proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When a party seeks a stay of a civil action alleging infringement in relation to a transitional proceeding, the court shall decide whether to enter a stay based on: (A) whether a stay or denial will simplify issues and streamline the trial; (B) whether discovery is complete and whether a trial date has been set; (C) whether a stay or denial would unduly prejudice the nonmoving party or present a clear tactical advantage for the moving party; and (D) whether a stay or denial will reduce the burden of litigation on the parties and on the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute also permits immediate interlocutory appeal to the Federal Circuit from the district court's stay decision, with review to ensure consistent application of precedent and such review may be de novo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of Construction re: patent-eligible subject matter (section 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this [transitional CBM] section shall be construed as amending or interpreting categories of patent-eligible subject matter set forth under section 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, elsewhere: 'Nothing in this section shall be construed to imply that other business methods are patentable or that other business-method patents are valid.' These are statutory clarifications limiting substantive eligibility impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Public Enterprise Fund: establishment, uses, and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish the 'United States Patent and Trademark Office Public Enterprise Fund' in the Treasury; fees collected under sections 41, 42, and 376 (and certain trademark fees) shall be deposited into the Fund and be available to the Director without fiscal year limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts in Fund may cover all expenses consistent with fee-use limitations, including administrative/operating expenses and commitments; annual report to Congress (within 60 days after fiscal year end) must (1) summarize operations including financial details and staff levels by major activity, (2) detail operating plan including specific expense and staff needs, (3) describe long-term modernization plans, (4) set forth progress toward modernization, and (5) include results of most recent audit. Director must also provide annual spending plan to Appropriations Committees within 30 days of fiscal year start and provide an independent annual audit conducted according to generally acceptable accounting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment and pay cap for administrative patent/trademark judges
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has the authority to fix the rate of basic pay for the administrative patent judges and administrative trademark judges at not greater than the rate of basic pay payable for Level III of the Executive Schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of a rate under this paragraph shall not be subject to the pay limitation of sections 5306(e) or 5373 of title 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity qualification and related rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for small-entity reduced fees is conditioned in relevant amendments by criteria such as: (a) gross income in prior calendar year not exceeding 3 times the most recently reported median household income (as reported by the Bureau of the Census); (b) exclusions such as applications filed in another country, certain provisional or international applications for which the basic national fee was not paid; (c) prior employment assignment exception (an applicant is not considered named on a previously filed application for purposes of one rule if the applicant assigned or is under obligation to assign rights as result of previous employment); and (d) foreign currency exchange-rate translation guidance for gross income not in U.S. dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These amendments replace or refine small-entity size/income tests and include rules for prior employment and currency conversion to determine eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on providing court facilities outside the District of Columbia
rubrics_metrics.description: The repeal made by the amendment shall not be construed to authorize the provision of any court facilities or administrative support services outside of the District of Columbia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A construction/limitation clarifying that statutory changes do not authorize physical provision of court facilities/administrative support beyond DC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee descriptions to include expanded activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend language to expand fee descriptions from 'filing, processing, issuing, and maintaining patent applications and patents' to 'filing, searching, examining, issuing, appealing, and maintaining patent applications and patents.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that USPTO fee structure contemplates searching, examining, and appeals as fee-covered activities.
